messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: suggest warning in manual
parts: I was playing around with a simple linear regression with 5 data points and 3 predictors (so the posterior for the betas is t_2, which has long tails and infinite variance. After the default 2000 iterations, Stan didn’t seem too far from convergence (R-hat was 1.0 for the betas, 1.1 for sigma, and 1.4 for lp__) but the estimates for the parameters (mean, se_mean, sd) were all over the map. At first I was freaked out, then I remembered that the posterior distribution has infinite variance so these aren’t such great summaries! This made me think that perhaps in the manual when we introduce the default print() display, we add a sentence in a footnote explaining that the mean, se_mean, and sd can’t be taken seriously when the posterior variance is infinite.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] suggest warning in manual (RStan/PyStan/CmdStan)
parts:
On Apr 2, 2014, at 11:15 AM, Andrew Gelman <gel...@stat.columbia.edu> wrote:

> ...in the manual when we introduce the default print() display, we add a sentence in a footnote explaining that the mean, se_mean, and sd can't be taken seriously when the posterior variance is infinite.


I made a note on the manual issue to add it to the CmdStan manual.
It should probably also go in the R and Python docs, but I didn't
think this quite warranted new issues.

We've been hoping to refactor the general parts of the manual
out into a separate document. First, I'm going to pull out all of
the CmdStan-related material and put that with CmdStan. What's left
will apply equally to RStan/PyStan/CmdStan --- basically what comes
out of the C++ API and our general practices w.r.t. posterior analysis
(which will increasingly move into the C++ API from RStan and PyStan
and CmdStan).

Then we need to pull back some of the descriptions that are only
in the CmdStan section so they can be shared across the different
interfaces. This is also where we'd put a description of all the
sampling algorithms.

- Bob

P.S. Don't you guys have a special footnote or something for this infinite
variance condition?
